scope: GUI-owned asynchronous Start preflight, pending Stop/close, same-GUI fresh restart and read-only connected MCP inspection with two virtual user pairs and two owned x64 probes. No routed input or attachment. Both GUI cohorts set close_to_tray=false.
implemented: GUI Start immediately owns one Controller; its supervisor performs authoritative device, profile, target, runtime, original-process identity and emergency-stop health checks off the UI thread. Synchronous Controller entry points retain validation for standalone MCP.

Stop is latched through preflight and identity installation. One owned controller/receiver remains until terminal, preventing overlapping launches or stale completion reuse. GUI ignores late nonterminal readiness after Stop.

Prepared watches are built off-lock. Cancellation before profile delivery drops untouched identities and yields clean Stopped; after delivery, existing worker/job/transport cleanup and quarantine remain authoritative.

Ouroboros Start/Pause/Stop and Starting/Stopping labels reflect pending state. Navigation and owner-requested normal close with close-to-tray disabled remain usable during the accepted cancellable diagnostic delay.

actual.cohort_a_restart: Same GUI, new pending controller then Ready/Running, scoped read-only agent_session/routing_state with two users, ordinary Stop and close.

image.note: Both fresh owned captures have identical pixels for the same configured names; distinct HWND/geometry and files are recorded.

limits: Native acceptance uses the bounded cooperative delay before preflight; it does not interrupt or establish cancellation timing inside arbitrary blocked Windows calls. Cancellation checks are between native phases.
Fresh validation and process scope were retained, not bypassed. Post-delivery failed cleanup and original-process quarantine remain required.

Raw Input capture startup, the historical GUI stall cause, general P1 reliability, hardware/RustDesk input, arbitrary application compatibility, mixed-DPI, benchmarks, full UX and Ultra parity remain open.
Standalone MCP Start retains its existing synchronous control semantics; no new tool, grant, pre-Ready GUI connection or generalized standalone Start cancellation is claimed.
